newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey Jan-Oct exports $19 bln, imports $34.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Turkey Jan-Oct exports $19 bln, imports $34.4 bln.

text.p: Turkish state minister Ayfer Ylmaz, in charge of foreign trade, said on Friday Turkey's January-October 1996 exports were estimated at $19 billion, and imports at $34.4 billion.

"According to provisional figures obtained from customs authorities, Turkey's imports are seen at $34.4 billion, and exports at $19 billion in the first ten months. We can see a 15 percent rise in exports," Ylmaz told a seminar held by the Treasury in Ankara.
Ylmaz said the figures were provisional and might show a deviation of five percent.
"But a decrease in textile exports, which has a 40 to 45 percent share in Turkey's total exports, must be taken into account," she added.
She said Turkey would encourage exports in 1997 to maintain the trade deficit at $20 billion.

"We were expecting a rise in import figures in 1996 (after the custom union with the European Union) and that especially occured in imports of investment goods. That shows we will see improvements in investment in coming years," she said.
Yilmaz also pointed at narrowing Turkish exports due to tight measures taken by European countries after the Maastrict agreement.
"But we can say there have been increases in exports of automotive, food and electronics sectors after the customs unions," Ylmaz said.

Turkey's trade deficit surged 88.4 percent to $3.95 billion in the first quarter of 1996 from the same 1995 period, according to official data which has been delayed due to technical problems arising from the customs union agreement.
The official 1996 deficit target is $16 billion, but senior officials have predicted it would reach more than $20 billion.
